title: China tightens IPO bar for humanoid robot startups as bubble fears mount in red-hot embodied AI sector
source_used: Business Upturn (relaying CNBC and Reuters reporting)
key_facts: China's securities regulator (CSRC) has given investment banks informal "window guidance" raising the bar for humanoid robot startups to list, three people familiar with its thinking told CNBC

Candidates are expected to show sustainable revenue and commercial orders, a path to narrower losses and core technology such as robot "brains" or advanced hands; one source said a three-year forecast may be required, another that two of three conditions may suffice
Reuters reported the move follows Unitree Robotics' volatile debut, with shares about 55 percent below their peak
Some sources describe humanoid IPOs as effectively frozen; others call it a sector-specific slowdown, not a ban
No formal rule change is on the CSRC website and the regulator has made no public statement
Concerns include revenue from related-party purchases and government-linked pilots
quote_evidence: The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) has conveyed stricter expectations to investment banks through "window guidance," three people familiar with the regulator's thinking told CNBC.
No formal rule change has been announced on the CSRC's website, and the regulator has not issued a public statement on the matter.
why_it_matters_hint: Beijing is cooling its hottest AI investment theme before more robot makers list on hype alone
event_date: Reported 3 Oct 2026; guidance timing not stated
notes: Business Upturn text rests on CNBC (three sources) and Reuters (Unitree); CNBC is the first reporter, so credited. CNBC URL not given in the article; url is the page read. Informal guidance, unconfirmed by the regulator.
